title: Personal Loans Refinance Pricing Memo: AutoPay-Record Credit on the Refinance Fee
content:
## Rule

An AutoPay credit comes off the refinance fee percent of a Personal Loans refinance application, counting the AutoPay debits posted on the loan being refinanced fewer than 12 whole months (whole calendar months being the difference in calendar months, less one when the later date's day of the month is smaller than the earlier date's) before the application date: 12 or more such debits with no AutoPay debit returned in those months earn 0.25 point; 6 to 11 such debits with none returned earn 0.1 point; any other loan earns no AutoPay credit. An AutoPay debit is any payment AutoPay took on the loan, a hardship plan payment included, and an AutoPay debit returned is a return of such a payment.

| AutoPay debits posted fewer than 12 whole months before | AutoPay debit returned in those months | Credit |
|---|---|---|
| 12 or more | none | 0.25 point |
| 6 to 11 | none | 0.10 point |
| any | one or more | none |
| 5 or fewer | none | none |

The refinance fee percent, with this credit taken off, never goes below zero.

## Cases (hypothetical records, application on 20 September)

- 12 AutoPay debits from 20 September of the year before to 20 August, none returned: the debit of 20 September of the year before is 12 whole months back and is not counted, leaving 11: 0.10 point.
- 12 AutoPay debits from 21 September of the year before onward, none returned: 12 counted: 0.25 point.
- 12 AutoPay debits with one of them returned in March: none.
- An AutoPay debit that paid a hardship plan installment counts as an AutoPay debit.
